mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 3% for two consecutive months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3.0 and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 20-day window, SPX 20d returns are not statistically different from the pre-inflation spike mean (p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL reverts below 3% within one month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS exceeding 10,000 jobs signals strengthening labor market demand, which precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Over 60 days, SPX 20d returns (aggregated into 60d) show no significant positive deviation from the prior 60-day mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly increase in HOUST (household spending) of at least 2% predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as consumer confidence drives equity valuation expansion.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 20-day windows following the trigger, 20d returns are negative or flat, and the 20-day moving average of HOUST growth is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of 2% or more indicates supply-side weakness, which is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by 2% or more for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified INDPRO contraction period.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 shows a negative 5-day forward return as investors anticipate tighter credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0 and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 5-day horizon, SPX 5d returns are not negative or flat (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% for two consecutive months, accompanied by a rise in PAYEMS, signals a tight labor market and supports a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 for two consecutive months AND PAYEMS increase
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns over the 60-day horizon are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in GDPC1 (GDP) growth (quarterly) below 1% for three quarters predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to risk-off sentiment.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth < 1% for three consecutive quarters
failure_condition: During the three-quarter GDPC1 contraction, SPX 20d returns are not persistently negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 5% month-over-month for two consecutive months in a post-recession regime, the S&P 500 exhibits a negative 20-day forward return as weak demand weighs on equities.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >5% for two consecutive months and regime is post-recession
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns during the trigger period are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
